disclosures.section: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements > Note 7: Restructuring and Other Charges
sections: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements > Note 7: Restructuring and Other Charges
disclosures.summary: Litigation charges in 2025 included a $163 million benefit from the reduction of a previously accrued EC-imposed fine, for which Intel funded a $340 million guarantee in legally restricted accounts due to the fine remaining unpaid on appeal; 2024 charges included $780 million from R2 litigation, while 2023 included a $1.2 billion benefit from VLSI litigation developments, a $353 million termination fee for the Tower acquisition, and a $401 million EC fine charge.
disclosures.content: Restructuring activities related to employee severance and benefit arrangements under the 2025, 2024 and 2022 Restructuring Plans were as follows: Litigation charges and other includes a $163 million benefit recorded in 2025 from the reduction of the previously accrued EC-imposed fine recorded in 2023. While the fine remains unpaid on appeal, our obligation is guaranteed by a third party. We funded the guarantee in 2025 by depositing $340 million in legally restricted accounts, for which the restricted cash is presented within other long-term assets. The 2024 charges include $780 million arising out of the R2 litigation. In 2023, a $1.2 billion benefit was recorded due to a reduction in a previously accrued charge as a result of developments in the VLSI litigation. The 2023 charges also included a $353 million termination fee in connection with our inability to timely obtain required regulatory approvals needed to acquire Tower in accordance with the contractual terms of the terminated acquisition agreement and a $401 million charge for the original EC-imposed fine.
